key_insight: LogCDM combines sequence surprise and behavioral graph drift for compact, interpretable log anomaly detection without GPU inference.
engineering_relevance: Its 8.1–8.8M parameters and 5.5–10.5 ms CPU latency per session make it a candidate for deployment on log-producing monitoring nodes.
method: Score next-event surprise with a small causal Transformer.
Compare session and normal-reference graph embeddings, and quantify transition drift using a frequency-weighted chi-squared divergence with per-edge explanations.
Fuse all three signals through a learned sigmoid gate.
evidence_signal: Reported F1 scores are 0.984 on HDFS, 0.870 on chronologically split BGL, and 0.850 on Thunderbird; structural signals add 0.025–0.030 F1 on BGL and Thunderbird but almost none on HDFS.
watch_item: Structural benefits vary by dataset, and the gate's Bayes-posterior interpretation depends on a shared-covariance Gaussian assumption.
paper_title: LogCDM: Interpretable Log Anomaly Detection via Behavioral Graph Drift and Adaptive Signal Fusion
